title: RULES ON THE OPERATION OF THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY LIBRARY
full_text:
RULES ON THE OPERATION OF THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY LIBRARY

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
These Rules prescribe matters delegated by the National Assembly Library Act and matters necessary for its implementation.

Article 2 (Opening and closing of the Library)
(1) The National Assembly Library (hereinafter referred to as the “Library”) shall open on the working days of public officials. However, it may also open on Saturdays and Sundays where the Chief Librarian of the National Assembly Library (hereinafter referred to as the “Chief Librarian”) considers this necessary to provide library services under Article 2(2) of the National Assembly Library Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Act”). <Amended on March 22, 2018>
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the Library may close periodically for such purposes as checking its holdings or changing its systems, or on a day the Chief Librarian considers necessary.
(3) The Chief Librarian shall separately determine the extent to which the Library opens under paragraph (1).

Article 3 (Standardization of the national bibliography)
To prepare and standardize the national bibliography under Article 2(1)5 of the Act, the Chief Librarian may exchange information on books and authors, and other information necessary for registering and issuing standard identifiers, including through agreements with domestic and overseas standards organizations.

CHAPTER II LIBRARY SERVICES <Amended on March 22, 2018>

Article 4 (Eligible users)
Persons eligible for library services under Article 2(2) of the Act shall be university students, persons aged 18 or older, and other persons whom the Chief Librarian recognizes as needing library materials. <Amended on March 22, 2018>

Article 5 (Reading hours)
Reading shall be limited to the working hours of public officials. However, the Chief Librarian may adjust reading hours where necessary for reading on Saturdays, Sundays, at night, or at other times.

Article 6 (Loans for use outside the Library)
(1) The following persons may borrow library materials for use outside the Library (hereinafter referred to as “loans”):
1. Members of the National Assembly and public officials belonging to the National Assembly.
2. Former members of the National Assembly or retired National Assembly public officials of vice-ministerial rank or higher who have been issued a reader's card.
3. Retired public officials with at least 20 years of service in the National Assembly, or persons whom the Chief Librarian recognizes as having rendered distinguished service to the Library, who have been issued a reader's card.
4. Other persons approved by the Chief Librarian.
(2) The following materials shall not be loaned. However, materials listed in subparagraphs 2 through 5 may be loaned with the Chief Librarian's permission where required for members of the National Assembly or its public officials to perform their duties:
1. Rare books and old books.
2. Reference books, loose-leaf collections of statutes, periodicals, newspapers, academic theses and dissertations, and National Assembly minutes.
3. Audiovisual materials and microform materials.
4. Domestic books for which no duplicate copy is held.
5. Other materials specified by the Chief Librarian.
(3) The Chief Librarian shall take necessary measures to prevent the loss of or damage to library materials loaned under paragraphs (1) and (2).

Article 7 (Loan limits and periods)
(1) The Chief Librarian shall separately determine loan limits and periods.
(2) Even during a loan period, the Chief Librarian may require the return of materials urgently needed to support the National Assembly's legislative activities.

CHAPTER III OPERATION OF BRANCH LIBRARIES <Added on March 22, 2018>

Article 8 (Functions of branch libraries)
Branch libraries may specialize in performing the Library's duties under Article 2(1) of the Act and provide user education, lectures, cultural events, library services, and other services.

Article 9 (Detailed operating rules)
Matters necessary for the operation of branch libraries, other than those prescribed in this Chapter, shall be determined by the Chief Librarian.

CHAPTER IV LEGAL DEPOSIT OF LIBRARY MATERIALS <Amended on March 22, 2018>

Article 10 (Materials subject to legal deposit)
(1) Library materials deposited under Article 7 of the Act shall be:
1. Books.
2. Master's theses and doctoral dissertations.
3. Periodicals.
4. Audiovisual materials, including compact discs and digital video discs.
5. Electronic materials, including digital files.
6. Other library materials recognized by the Chief Librarian, including materials published in new forms as publishing conditions change and information technology develops.
(2) “Library materials prescribed by the Rules” in Article 7(2) of the Act means materials submitted to the National Assembly by State agencies, local governments, public institutions and organizations, and educational and research institutions; other materials the Chief Librarian considers necessary to support legislative activities; and materials suitable as exchange publications to promote and support international cooperation.

Article 11 (Deposit procedures and cooperation in providing materials)
(1) For library materials under Article 7(1) of the Act submitted to the National Assembly or a committee, the Chief Librarian may request their provision from the National Assembly Secretariat or the relevant committee. <Amended on March 22, 2018>
(2) A person other than a State agency, local government, public institution or organization, or educational or research institution wishing to deposit materials shall submit an itemized statement of the materials in advance. After examining it, the Chief Librarian may reduce the number of copies to be deposited or decline to accept the deposit. <Amended on March 22, 2018>

Article 12 (Deposit Compensation Deliberation Committee)
(1) A Deposit Compensation Deliberation Committee (hereinafter referred to as the “Deliberation Committee”) shall be established to deliberate on the following matters concerning compensation for library materials deposited under Article 7(3) of the Act:
1. Compensation rates for the legal deposit of library materials.
2. Changes to compensation amounts for legal deposit.
3. Payment of fees for services performed by legal-deposit agents.
4. Other matters that its chairperson considers necessary and refers to a meeting.
(2) Other matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Deliberation Committee shall be determined by the Chief Librarian.

Article 13 (Compensation procedures)
(1) A person who has deposited library materials under Article 7(3) of the Act and wishes to receive compensation shall claim compensation from the Chief Librarian within 90 days after the deposit.
(2) Upon receiving a claim under paragraph (1), the Chief Librarian shall pay compensation at the rate designated annually by the Deliberation Committee, within the market value of the materials. For materials bearing a fixed price under Article 22 of the Publishing Industry Promotion Act, that fixed price shall be deemed their market value.
(3) Notwithstanding paragraph (2), where the Chief Librarian considers that the market value differs considerably from the ordinary transaction price of similar materials, or that compensation based on market value is otherwise unreasonable, the Chief Librarian may determine the compensation amount after deliberation by the Deliberation Committee, taking into account the ordinary transaction prices of similar materials and other relevant factors.
(4) A person objecting to an amount determined under paragraph (3) may file an objection with the Chief Librarian, specifying concrete grounds, within 30 days after being notified of the amount.
(5) Within 30 days after receiving an objection under paragraph (4), the Chief Librarian shall, after deliberation by the Deliberation Committee, redetermine and notify the compensation amount if the objection is well founded, or notify the claimant that it is unfounded if it lacks grounds.

Article 14 (Legal-deposit agents and fees)
(1) To process legal-deposit work efficiently, the Chief Librarian may select a business operator contracted with the Library to act as a legal-deposit agent (hereinafter referred to as a “deposit agent”) and have it perform deposit work under Article 7 of the Act. In such cases, fees for the agency services shall be paid within budgetary limits.
(2) Where a deposit agent under paragraph (1) deposits materials more than 30 days after publication or production, the Chief Librarian may vary the agency fee after deliberation by the Deliberation Committee.

CHAPTER V ESTABLISHMENT OF A HUMAN RESOURCE INFORMATION NETWORK <Added on March 22, 2018>

Article 15 (Establishment and operation of a human resource information network)
Under Article 8 of the Act, the Chief Librarian may collect human resource information on members of the National Assembly and experts in various fields and establish and operate a database.

Article 16 (Collection of human resource information)
(1) To establish and operate the database under Article 15, the Chief Librarian may collect and provide the following human resource information in accordance with the Personal Information Protection Act:
1. Personal information, including name, photograph, date of birth, gender, occupation, affiliation, position, educational background, address, telephone number, and email address.
2. Research-field information, including field of expertise, subfield, and research keywords.
3. Information on activities and achievements, including career, publications, external activities, and awards and honors.
(2) Upon a request from the subject of the human resource information, the Chief Librarian shall correct or delete the information under management.

CHAPTER VI EXCHANGE, TRANSFER, DISPOSAL, AND REMOVAL OF LIBRARY MATERIALS FROM THE CATALOGUE <Amended on March 22, 2018>

Article 17 (Exchange and transfer)
(1) Materials that may be exchanged with or transferred to other libraries and similar bodies shall be: <Amended on March 22, 2018>
1. Unused duplicate copies exceeding the number needed.
2. Unneeded materials whose use is considered more efficient if management is transferred to another library or similar body.
3. Other materials determined by the Chief Librarian.
(2) Procedures and methods for exchange or transfer shall comply with the statutes and regulations on the management of government goods. <Amended on March 22, 2018>

Article 18 (Disposal and removal from the catalogue)
(1) The Chief Librarian may dispose of:
1. Materials considered no longer necessary to preserve because they have lost their usefulness.
2. Materials considered difficult to use or impossible to repair because they are soiled or unusable.
3. Duplicate materials considered unnecessary to preserve because, for example, a full-text database has been established.
(2) The department responsible for preserving materials and providing access shall examine the materials under paragraph (1) and, where disposal is necessary, report a disposal plan to the Chief Librarian. Annual disposal shall not exceed five percent of the Library's total holdings. <Amended on March 22, 2018>
(3) Before disposing of materials under paragraph (1), the Chief Librarian shall report the list of materials to the House Steering Committee of the National Assembly.
(4) Materials lost because of natural disasters, accidents beyond control, or other similar causes may be removed from the catalogue. <Amended on March 22, 2018>

CHAPTER VII ADVISORY COMMITTEE ON DEVELOPMENT OF THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY LIBRARY <Amended on March 22, 2018>

Article 19 (Composition)
(1) The Advisory Committee on Development of the National Assembly Library under Article 10 of the Act (hereinafter in this Chapter referred to as the “Committee”) shall consist of no more than 30 members, including one chairperson.
(2) Where the nature of an agenda item requires it, the chairperson may establish and operate a subcommittee of no more than 10 members.
(3) Members shall be commissioned or appointed by the Chief Librarian from among outside persons with extensive knowledge and experience in library affairs or National Assembly public officials.
(4) Members shall elect the chairperson from among themselves. Where the chairperson is unable to act, a member designated by the Chief Librarian shall act in the chairperson's place.
(5) The Committee shall have one secretary, appointed by the Chief Librarian from among Library public officials.
(6) Members shall serve for two years and may be reappointed.

Article 20 (Functions)
The Committee shall advise the Chief Librarian on:
1. Basic policies for the development of the Library and its operation.
2. The structure of the Library's information cooperation network and the adjustment and overall coordination of its functions.
3. Library informatization, including establishment of the digital library.
4. Other matters that the Chief Librarian considers necessary for the Library's development and refers to a meeting.

Article 21 (Duties)
(1) The chairperson shall preside over the Committee and oversee its affairs.
(2) Under the chairperson's direction, the secretary shall handle the affairs of the Committee and its subcommittees.

Article 22 (Meetings)
(1) The chairperson shall convene the Committee where the chairperson considers it necessary or the Chief Librarian requests it.
(2) Meetings shall open with more than half of the members present, and decisions shall be adopted by the affirmative vote of more than half of those present.

Article 23 (Allowances)
Members attending meetings of the Committee or its subcommittees may be paid allowances within budgetary limits.

Article 24 (Detailed operating rules)
Other matters necessary for the operation of the Committee or its subcommittees, beyond those prescribed in this Chapter, shall be determined by the Chief Librarian.

CHAPTER VIII SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS <Amended on March 22, 2018>

Article 25 (Delegation)
Other matters necessary for the operation of the Library beyond these Rules shall be separately determined by the Chief Librarian.

ADDENDUM <No. 153, February 24, 2010>
These Rules shall enter into force on the date they are adopted by the House Steering Committee of the National Assembly.

ADDENDA <No. 213, March 22, 2018>
Article 1 (Effective date)
These Rules shall enter into force on the date they are adopted by the House Steering Committee of the National Assembly.
Article 2 (Application concerning compensation for library materials)
The amended Article 13 shall apply to library materials deposited with the Library after these Rules enter into force.
